# Reviewer application

## Project and requested outcome

TokenJunkieLabs is building open-source, self-hostable software that lets a merchant sell a useful API, dataset or agent operation on Stellar and lets the buyer receive the complete result in its existing application.

We request **$38,000 for 400 prospective delivery hours over 150 days from award acceptance**. The outcome is two independently operated merchant services, each used by an independent buyer, with two independent buyer operators and the same useful service operating through two independently operated facilitators. The work progresses from installed services by day 30 to recurring testnet use by day 90 and maintainable mainnet operation by day 150.

A purchase connects four records: the buyer’s approved request, the settled transfer, the complete usable output and the merchant’s fulfillment or accounting. The application keeps that connection through interrupted delivery, a changed source edition and transfer to another maintainer.

The existing product is the starting point. The award funds reusable Stellar integration, source and receiving adaptations, deployment, monitoring and recovery improvements required by the selected independent services. Those improvements return to the public product.

## Customer problem, need and adoption

Our first customer is a recurring API/data-service operator or the agency implementing that service in its customer’s application. The commissioning payer buys the installation and maintainable handover; the independent buyer pays for the useful resource. These roles can belong to different organizations.

An analyst needs the complete selected population, source period, units and usable report. An agent application needs the result it approved and control over aggregate spending. A prepaid customer’s saved call must keep its selected pass and consumed allowance when defaults change. The merchant needs to connect payment, complete output, its offer and later service or accounting obligations.

Public implementation reports illustrate the gap: a merchant’s payment-bearing calls failed across a GET/POST mismatch; another reported successful settlement with missing Bazaar indexing. These Base reports supply cross-ecosystem implementation learning for our Stellar request, discovery and receiving integration. [Method report](https://github.com/x402-foundation/x402/issues/3657) · [Discovery report](https://github.com/x402-foundation/x402/issues/3677).

Our own conversations establish commissioning decisions:

|Veridex|Invited an open testnet design partnership after declining a third-party testing budget. The proposed route/buyer adaptation is $1,500 over five business days; payer agreement remains open.|
|CoCart|Its founder asked who introduces and pays for the customer work, how referral compensation works and who contracts. The proposed $7,200 / 60-hour / fifteen-business-day workshare covers one customer’s headless cart, checkout, payment/order operation and receiving.|

TokenJunkieLabs sells defined implementation and separately scoped care; merchants retain their resource receipts. Delivery effort, corrections, support time and collections inform later pricing. Customer benefit is less active effort and fewer manual corrections from approved purchase to useful output, with a service another engineer can operate.

## Why Stellar and what we contribute

Stellar supplies the settlement for the operation the buyer approved. Each approval binds the request to its network, asset, recipient and integer atomic amount. The native Stellar SDK and selected facilitator verify and settle that authorization. The application associates the returned settlement with the original request, complete output and merchant action. The buyer retains signing and aggregate spending authority; the merchant controls its resource and terms.

We compose the existing x402 Exact Stellar scheme, SDKs, token contracts and facilitators, including the selected provider’s actual payment requirements and optional discovery extension. The existing MPP Charge integration retains its own challenge and recovery model.

There are close alternatives. [ApiCharge](https://communityfund.stellar.org/project/apicharge-djv) combines service publication and consumption with Soroban settlement and signed agreements. [Nirium](https://github.com/nirium-protocol/nirium) provides Stellar payment SDKs, seller middleware, MCP and CLI interfaces. [MPP Router](https://www.mpprouter.dev/how-it-works) supplies service discovery and paid calls; [Stellar Raven](https://raven.stellar.org/docs) supplies ecosystem context and integration operations through MCP. Our application completes the customer’s continuing operation around payment: source review, complete paginated or file output, receiving into its business application, interrupted-operation recovery, and transfer of the working service to another maintainer.

We propose [Open Track](https://stellar.gitbook.io/scf-handbook/scf-awards/build-award/open-track) for this reusable merchant-and-buyer operating application. The funded contribution is the source-to-result and receiving workflow across independent services, with published implementation and deployment improvements. The same-service, two-facilitator deliverable includes the required registration and payment-policy integration. The retained catalogue comparison found 27 Vellar offers and two Periplo offers with no shared seller/route identity, so this package includes real same-service registration and compatibility. Repeat independent purchases and successfully operated customer installations measure the value to Stellar.

## Defined architecture and operating behavior

The architecture has six components: a private merchant source/release workspace; its public HTTP or MCP operation; the Stellar SDK and facilitator; private buyer approval and spending state; retained delivery records and complete output; and merchant fulfillment/accounting.

1. **Select and publish.** The merchant chooses an authorized source edition or named live query, schema, output and limits. Review resolves the route, network, asset, recipient, amount and authorization lifetime. Later source or terms changes become separately reviewed states.
2. **Connect the source.** Adapters preserve types, null values, pagination, keys, units, time basis and snapshot/live behavior. Customer-controlled credential or OAuth references select access. The returned result identifies its source edition.
3. **Approve and pay.** The buyer retains the HTTP method or MCP tool, arguments, scope and payment option. The remote schema and full challenge, including authorization lifetime, must match before signing. For paid MCP, the endpoint, tool and arguments remain separate from the payment resource; the official MCP SDK carries payment and settlement metadata. Per-payment limits and the existing reservation/budget owner govern aggregate spending.
4. **Settle and receive.** The facilitator verifies and settles the native authorization. Independent RPC reconciliation checks the network, asset, parties and atomic amount. The application retains the complete output, merchant notification and receiving acknowledgment. A multi-request acquisition keeps its aggregate cost and unfinished coverage. Saved prepaid calls retain their selected pass; a replacement links to its predecessor and acquired results remain available.
5. **Use and account.** The receiving application opens every page and file needed for the task. Merchant pricing connects the selected tariff and saved uniform quote to an actual usage period, counting basis and supplier-cost basis. A reviewed price change carries its measured source into the customer quotation and original invoice or service records.
6. **Recover and hand over.** Server confirmation, observed transfer, output and fulfillment retain separate states. An uncertain signed response is reconciled through its original dispatch. The receiving engineer restores configuration, history and customer files, supplies authorized secret references and continues the same operation.

Node.js supplies the merchant, buyer, browser, CLI, typed-client and MCP interfaces. Source adapters and receiving applications retain their native semantics. The maintained implementation also uses Python and SQLite for typed data and saved queries, and PHP for WordPress/WooCommerce integration. New contracts are outside this six-package request; the product uses existing SDKs and token contracts.

### Turn reported observations into a retained decision

The observation review preserves the producer's reported values and source context. A completed run, a failed assertion and that assertion's warning severity remain separate facts in the review. An omitted measurement stays unreported; a reported zero keeps its original meaning. The original containing record remains available when the producer uses a source contract that the adapter cannot interpret.

An operator can save a metric rule for an exact reported field, or a named assertion rule for the exact assertion and optional column. Each rule identifies the dataset, facet scope, severity, enabled state and treatment of missing observations. Metric comparisons use finite thresholds or an inclusive range. A revised or disabled rule retains its earlier versions, and an existing evaluation retains the versions used to produce it.

Evaluation previews bind to the currently selected workspace revision, edition, dataset and run. Saving from the browser also binds the exact source-selection and rule-set hashes returned with the displayed preview. If another action changes the selection or revision, the operator reviews the current state before saving the retained intent. A saved evaluation preserves its full findings, expected and actual values, original event and observation identities, source locations and selected rules.

The operator then records a reasoned disposition against a specific finding in that saved evaluation: open, investigating, accepted or resolved. Each update preserves earlier decisions and the original finding. A subsequent producer event supports a subsequent evaluation, so the receiving engineer can inspect both the earlier result and the later correction. Supporting files can accompany that history through the application's existing complete result-attachment workflow.

The recurring deliverable includes the complete selected originals, applicable dataset-rule versions, saved evaluations, reasoned findings and reports alongside the service-level assessment. JSON retains the structured evaluation; CSV carries its findings into ordinary spreadsheet work; HTML presents the review in a readable report. The editable handover retains the earlier source editions, rules, findings and decisions so the receiving engineer can inspect a correction and continue the next review.

Project and requested outcome

TokenJunkieLabs is building open-source, self-hostable software that lets a merchant sell a useful API, dataset or agent operation on Stellar and lets the buyer receive the complete result in its existing application.

We request $38,000 for 400 prospective delivery hours over 150 days from award acceptance. The outcome is two independently operated merchant services, each used by an independent buyer, with two independent buyer operators and the same useful service operating through two independently operated facilitators. The work progresses from installed services by day 30 to recurring testnet use by day 90 and maintainable mainnet operation by day 150.

A purchase connects four records: the buyer’s approved request, the settled transfer, the complete usable output and the merchant’s fulfillment or accounting. The application keeps that connection through interrupted delivery, a changed source edition and transfer to another maintainer.

The existing product is the starting point. The award funds reusable Stellar integration, source and receiving adaptations, deployment, monitoring and recovery improvements required by the selected independent services. Those improvements return to the public product.

Why Stellar and what we contribute

Stellar supplies the settlement for the operation the buyer approved. Each approval binds the request to its network, asset, recipient and integer atomic amount. The native Stellar SDK and selected facilitator verify and settle that authorization. The application associates the returned settlement with the original request, complete output and merchant action. The buyer retains signing and aggregate spending authority; the merchant controls its resource and terms.

We compose the existing x402 Exact Stellar scheme, SDKs, token contracts and facilitators, including the selected provider’s actual payment requirements and optional discovery extension. The existing MPP Charge integration retains its own challenge and recovery model.

There are close alternatives. ApiCharge combines service publication and consumption with Soroban settlement and signed agreements. Nirium provides Stellar payment SDKs, seller middleware, MCP and CLI interfaces. MPP Router supplies service discovery and paid calls; Stellar Raven supplies ecosystem context and integration operations through MCP. Our application completes the customer’s continuing operation around payment: source review, complete paginated or file output, receiving into its business application, interrupted-operation recovery, and transfer of the working service to another maintainer.

We propose Open Track for this reusable merchant-and-buyer operating application. The funded contribution is the source-to-result and receiving workflow across independent services, with published implementation and deployment improvements. The same-service, two-facilitator deliverable includes the required registration and payment-policy integration. The retained catalogue comparison found 27 Vellar offers and two Periplo offers with no shared seller/route identity, so this package includes real same-service registration and compatibility. Repeat independent purchases and successfully operated customer installations measure the value to Stellar.

Defined architecture and operating behavior

The architecture has six components: a private merchant source/release workspace; its public HTTP or MCP operation; the Stellar SDK and facilitator; private buyer approval and spending state; retained delivery records and complete output; and merchant fulfillment/accounting.

  1. Select and publish. The merchant chooses an authorized source edition or named live query, schema, output and limits. Review resolves the route, network, asset, recipient, amount and authorization lifetime. Later source or terms changes become separately reviewed states.
  2. Connect the source. Adapters preserve types, null values, pagination, keys, units, time basis and snapshot/live behavior. Customer-controlled credential or OAuth references select access. The returned result identifies its source edition.
  3. Approve and pay. The buyer retains the HTTP method or MCP tool, arguments, scope and payment option. The remote schema and full challenge, including authorization lifetime, must match before signing. For paid MCP, the endpoint, tool and arguments remain separate from the payment resource; the official MCP SDK carries payment and settlement metadata. Per-payment limits and the existing reservation/budget owner govern aggregate spending.
  4. Settle and receive. The facilitator verifies and settles the native authorization. Independent RPC reconciliation checks the network, asset, parties and atomic amount. The application retains the complete output, merchant notification and receiving acknowledgment. A multi-request acquisition keeps its aggregate cost and unfinished coverage. Saved prepaid calls retain their selected pass; a replacement links to its predecessor and acquired results remain available.
  5. Use and account. The receiving application opens every page and file needed for the task. Merchant pricing connects the selected tariff and saved uniform quote to an actual usage period, counting basis and supplier-cost basis. A reviewed price change carries its measured source into the customer quotation and original invoice or service records.
  6. Recover and hand over. Server confirmation, observed transfer, output and fulfillment retain separate states. An uncertain signed response is reconciled through its original dispatch. The receiving engineer restores configuration, history and customer files, supplies authorized secret references and continues the same operation.

Node.js supplies the merchant, buyer, browser, CLI, typed-client and MCP interfaces. Source adapters and receiving applications retain their native semantics. The maintained implementation also uses Python and SQLite for typed data and saved queries, and PHP for WordPress/WooCommerce integration. New contracts are outside this six-package request; the product uses existing SDKs and token contracts.
